meanings.note: polite, or to several people; the first в is silent

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Core Russian name meaning 'Anisimov' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Это слово «анисимов» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'Anisimov' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
Look it up on the internet.
Look it up on the internet.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fix, to repair', paired with 'починить'.

examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: fleeting е in all declined forms: отца, отцу...

examples.trans: The Godfather is a famous film.

examples.text: Твой отец когда-то назвал меня очкариком.
examples.trans: Your father once called me four-eyes.

meanings.en: to offend, to hurt someone's feelings
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'идеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offend, to hurt', paired with 'обижать'.

examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.
He didn't want to offend anyone.

examples.text: Извини, я не хотела обидеть. А ты что здесь делаешь?
examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you. And what are you doing here?

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Осторожно, ты пронзил меня своей колбасой!
examples.trans: Careful, you impaled me with your sausage!

examples.text: Обидишь Настю, я из тебя колбасу сделаю.
examples.trans: If you hurt Nastya, I will turn you into sausage.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: in a mistaken or improper manner

examples.text: Луи, ты меня совсем неправильно понял!

meanings.note: понял? = got it?; понял = got it

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
